text.hook:
"std::set uses operator== to find duplicates."
That answer fails C++ interviews.

The map and set mental model, plus 6 myths. Swipe ➜ and save it. 💡
text.body:
Inside:
1. A tree with a comparator that decides identity
2. The insertion family, side by side
3. The comparator contract
4. Heterogeneous lookup with std::less<>
5. extract, merge and the alternatives
6. Six myths, busted (slides 8-9)

Which myth did you believe? Comment the slide number.

slides.hero:
std::map and std::set:
the mental model
+ 6 myths
slides.lead: A sorted tree where the comparator, not `operator==`, decides which keys are the same.

slides.title: A tree ordered by a comparator

cards.label: Red-black tree
cards.text: O(log n) find, insert, erase. Each level is a pointer dereference, often a cache miss.

cards.label: Equivalence
cards.text: Keys are the same when `!comp(a, b) && !comp(b, a)`. `operator==` is never called.

cards.label: Const keys
cards.text: `value_type` is `pair<const K, V>`: changing a key would break the order.

slides.takeaway: libstdc++, x86-64: a `map<int, int>` node is 40 bytes, plus allocator overhead.

slides.title: When the key already exists
slides.takeaway: Insert if absent: `try_emplace`. Insert or overwrite: `insert_or_assign`.

slides.title: A strict weak ordering
slides.warn: Broken by NaN keys and tolerance-based compares. The result is UB, not a slower map.
slides.takeaway: Compound keys: `std::tie(...) < std::tie(...)` or C++20 `operator<=> = default`.

cards.label: The problem
cards.text: With `map<string, int>`, `find(sv)` does not compile and `find("lit")` builds a `std::string`.

cards.label: extract
cards.text: Unlinks a node with no copy and no allocation. Returns a node handle.

cards.label: Change a key
cards.text: `nh.key() = new_key;` then `m.insert(std::move(nh))`. The only legal way.

cards.label: merge
cards.text: `dst.merge(src)` splices nodes. Keys already in `dst` stay in `src`.

slides.title: map is not always the answer
rows: ordered iteration, range queries, stable references
slides.takeaway: For tens of elements, a contiguous scan often beats a tree walk.

items.truth: It uses equivalence under the comparator: `!comp(a, b) && !comp(b, a)`.

items.myth: "`emplace` does nothing when the key exists."
items.truth: It may already have moved its arguments. `try_emplace` never does.

items.myth: "`std::lower_bound` on a map is O(log n)."
items.truth: O(log n) comparisons, O(n) iterator steps. Use the member `m.lower_bound(k)`.

items.myth: "A key can change through an iterator if the order stays the same."
"Heterogeneous lookup works with the default comparator."
items.truth: It needs a transparent comparator such as `std::less<>`.

items.myth: "O(log n) map always beats an O(n) vector scan."
items.truth: Not for small n: locality and branch prediction dominate.

slides.lead: Save this. Follow for a C++ interview puzzle every day.

text.hook:
Only checking stock. Nothing is written.
So the map cannot grow. Right?

Lock in your answer below, then swipe ➜ to verify.
text.body: One map, three lookups, one size at the end.

slides.title:
Read-only check.
What does it print?

slides.verdict_sub: The "read-only" check inserted pear and plum
bullets: `stock[name]` on a missing key **inserts** `{name, 0}` and returns a reference to it.
So the loop added two products with zero stock that nobody created.
`operator[]` does not even compile on a `const` map, a hint that it may modify.

slides.title: Read with find
slides.tip: Yes/no only: `contains` (C++20). Missing is an error: `at`, which throws.
slides.takeaway: `operator[]` is find-or-insert. Never use it for a pure read.

text.hook:
Sort orders by price, highest first: a.price >= b.price.
Tests with distinct prices pass. Then 40 orders share one price.

Lock in your answer below, then swipe ➜ to verify.
text.body: No compiler warning. The comparator reads naturally.

slides.title:
40 equal prices.
What happens?

slides.verdict_sub: Our GCC 11 run aborted: `free(): invalid size`. ASan: `heap-buffer-overflow`
bullets: A comparator must be a strict weak ordering: `comp(a, a)` must be false. With `>=` it is true.
libstdc++'s partition uses the pivot as a sentinel. It never stops on an equal element and scans past the end.
It shows up only with many equal keys (17 or more in libstdc++), so tests with distinct prices pass.

slides.title: Strictly before: `>`, never `>=`
slides.tip: `stable_sort` also keeps equal-price orders in arrival order.
slides.takeaway: `<=` in a `std::set` is UB too: libstdc++ inserts duplicates it then cannot find.

text.hook:
Greatest key <= k: lower_bound, then step back once.
Works for 25. Ship it?

Lock in your answer below, then swipe ➜ to verify.
text.body: Two calls, one of them a key that exists.

slides.title:
Greatest key `<= k`.
What does it print?

slides.verdict_sub: The second answer is wrong: 20 exists, so it should be 20
bullets: `lower_bound(k)` is the first key **not less** than `k`: `>= k`.
For 25 it returns 30, one step back gives 20: correct.
For 20 it returns 20 itself, one step back gives 10: wrong.
For any `k < 10` it returns `begin()`, and `--it` is UB.
slides.wrong: "20 20: lower_bound means first key below k"

slides.title: Step back from upper_bound
slides.takeaway: lower_bound = first not before `k`. upper_bound = first after `k`.

text.hook:
A range-for over a map with the pair type spelled out.
No auto, very explicit. And a pointer to the value.

Lock in your answer below, then swipe ➜ to verify.
text.body: One word is missing from the loop variable's type.

slides.title: Is this well-defined?

slides.verdict_sub: ASan: `stack-use-after-scope`. A plain GCC 11 run printed 42 by luck
bullets: The element type is `std::pair<const std::string, int>`, with a **const** key.
`e` cannot bind to it directly, so each iteration builds a converted temporary pair (copying the string).
`p` points into that temporary, which dies at the end of the iteration.
GCC warns with `-Wall`: `-Wrange-loop-construct`, "binds to a temporary".
slides.wrong: "Prints 42: e refers to the element in the map"

slides.title: Let auto spell the type
slides.tip: Spelled out correctly it is `const std::pair<const std::string, int>&`.
slides.takeaway: A map's element is `pair<const K, V>`. Iterate with `const auto&`.
